# Genesis Apocryphon Column 5 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Genesis Apocryphon Column 5 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 5:3 — "from his seed" vs "born from his own seed"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "from his seed" | Bare literal |
| LOGOS | "from his own seed" | Formal with possessive emphasis |
| PNEUMA | "born from his own seed" | Dynamic addition of "born" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "from his own seed." The possessive emphasis is implicit in context; PNEUMA's "born" is redundant.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 5:7 — "righteous one" vs "righteous man"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the righteous-one" | Hyphenated substantive |
| LOGOS | "the righteous one" | Formal substantive |
| PNEUMA | "a righteous man among you" | Dynamic with added "man" and "among you" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "the righteous one for you." PNEUMA adds words not in the fragment; the substantive adjective is standard.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 5:8 — "repose" vs "comfort" vs "relief"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a rest and a repose" | Literal pair preserving Aramaic nuach/niyach wordplay |
| LOGOS | "a rest and a comfort" | Formal rendering |
| PNEUMA | "bringing rest and relief" | Dynamic verbal construction |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "a rest and a comfort." Preserves the noun pair; "comfort" better serves English readers than "repose." The Noah/rest wordplay is noted but need not be forced.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 5:10 — "on" vs "upon" vs "coming upon"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a great destruction on the earth" | Literal preposition |
| LOGOS | "a great destruction upon the earth" | Formal with "upon" |
| PNEUMA | "a great devastation is coming upon the earth" | Dynamic with "devastation" and "coming" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "a great destruction upon the earth." "Upon" is more suited to prophetic register; PNEUMA's "devastation" and "coming" over-interpret the fragment.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 5:15 — "perfect" vs "blameless" vs "man of integrity"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the perfect-one" | Literal tamim |
| LOGOS | "the blameless one" | Standard biblical rendering of tamim |
| PNEUMA | "the man of integrity" | Dynamic paraphrase |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "the blameless one." This is the established biblical rendering of tamim (cf. Gen 6:9); PNEUMA's paraphrase is too free; EMET's "perfect" overstates the Aramaic.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

*Total disagreements: 5*
*Resolution: LOGOS 5, EMET 0, PNEUMA 0, Compromise 0*
